summary:
TOPIC: Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map


ABOUT OUR PROJECT: Vespera is a Mars Survival Guide whose Marswalk planner turns your science objective, routing mode, slope safety, season and duration into a 2D mission debrief map and then a 3D Mars simulation. It is built on NASA data, including rover POV photographs from Curiosity and Perseverance, so you can see Gale and Jezero Craters as the rovers did. Hazard warnings flag risky ground such as steep slopes, shown across NASA-sourced map layers, and a stats page wraps up your mission at the end.



AI USAGE: we used Claude and Gemini AI for our code production. 


TEAM:
1. Sohani: Lead Interface and Design Architect
2. Tanishi: Lead Terrain and 3D Engineer
3. Om: Director of Trajectory and Resources
4. Nivriti: Chief of Red Planet Research
details:
Vespera is a browser-based Mars spacewalk planner. You pick a science goal, and it builds a safe walking route across real NASA/USGS terrain at Jezero or Gale Crater, estimates the astronaut's workload and life-support cost, and lets you walk the route in 3D.

Currently, all information on Mars exists as separate entities. There are maps, with different levels of information, such as mineralogical, topographic and atmospheric maps. The problem is, real astronauts training for marswalks cannot rely on this information alone.

Vespera tackles this problem by integrating multiple datasets into a single map. It showcases how these different variables affect each other, while also factoring in components like gravity, speed and oxygen consumption.

Vespera accepts inputs such as mission objective, atmospheric condition, preferred time duration, slope steepness and routing modes to calculate the best possible path for your marswalk using the Dijkstra pathfinding algorithm.

It then gives you a hyper-specific mission objective, tailored exactly to the route.

It then makes use of the Pandolf–Santee metabolic equation at Mars gravity to give oxygen, water and power use. That is turned into Equivalent System Mass (ESM) and a dollar cost.

The 3D Marswalk feature brings together all of these components into a single environment. It makes use of real NASA elevation data to generate what the terrain would look like to an astronaut on Mars. It simulates gravity and walking speed. The 3D map contains toggleable layers showcasing visual, topographic, mineralogical and atmospheric data. Vespera gives you real time hazard warnings when you enter dangerous areas, having steep slopes, difficult terrain or dust storms. It simulates dust storms, and gives you survival tips to get through them safely.

The environment tracks the distance travelled and makes use of rover imagery and NASA information so that users can learn more about specific landmarks. It lets you view 3D models of rovers obtained from NASA 3D Resources.

After completing the marswalk, the statistics page displays your total distance travelled, elevation gain and loss, time in dust, and consumables used. This gives users an idea of what to expect on a real marswalk.

Overall, the main aim of Vespera is to bring separate datasets into one comprehensive environment, which serves not only as a map, but also as a survival guide for the Mars-trekkers of the future.

*This website is best experienced on a desktop browser for full 3D performance

Tools Used:

HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Three.js, Python

Data Used:

- USGS/NASA PDS elevation models (CTX DTM, MSL Gale DEM)

- NASA Mars Trek CTX imagery

- MRO CRISM mineral data

- Curiosity REMS pressure data

- NASA/JPL MMGIS rover traverses

- NASA Image Library photos

- NASA 3D rover models

Usage of SI:

We used Claude (Anthropic) and Google Gemini as AI coding assistants, and it wrote most of the code. Our team decided the concept, the mission-planning and pathfinding logic and the user experience. We chose and sourced the NASA/USGS datasets and the scientific models (Pandolf–Santee metabolic equations, NASA slope limits, ESM costing). We directed the AI feature by feature, tested every page, found and fixed bugs, and made the design decisions.

SI was used to bring our creative visualizations and concepts to life.
